newsitem.title: FRANCE: French capital markets closing report.
newsitem.headline: French capital markets closing report.

text.p: French bond futures finished MATIF trading higher at 131.00 in a session supported by firm T-Bonds ahead of news from the U.S. FOMC monetary policy council and helped back in Europe by a drop in German industry orders.

With one eye on the U.S. and expectations that the Federal Reserves council will leave rates alone, the market responded positively to a 1.4 percent drop in German industry orders in December, traders said.

"Even if the market's balancing on the sword of Damocles with the U.S. rates issue, it's focusing heavily on European news," said Sogeposte analyst Rachid Medjaoui, adding that he is not expecting a rate rise by the FOMC, whose meeting finishes this evening.
"The dollar rise is an opportunity for the U.S. and European economies," keeping the U.S. economy under control and giving European economies a breath of fresh air, he said.
Like others, he said the day's data highlighted fragility there and helped the market, combined with a rumour that German unemployment data on Thursday could come in very high.
Rachid Medjaoui was referring to talk that the jobless number for January could show a rise of 100,000, far more than the 40,000 people have been talking of so far.

European markets were also shaken by the renewed "will it, won't it" debates on European monetary union after a Financial Times report that there could be an agreement to delay the lira's joining the euro group, which was then denied in Brussels and several other European government centres, he said.
